verificationMode: offline; existing local source bytes and artifacts only
scope: Independent review of the KSH nationwide name inventory, raw/corrected country OSM extraction, existing manual review, and the completed three-city physical-cell prototype.

conclusion.status: Complete import of the pinned national KSH name source and country OSM snapshot; urban-quarter coverage remains incomplete and partly unknown. Existing manual candidates require review. Physical-cell results remain quarantined research.

independentComparison.normalization: Source strings have outer whitespace stripped; KSH codes and category codes are zero-padded. Twelve source rows contain outer whitespace. Municipality identity, source row and legal status, and every part source row, code, municipality name, part name, category, postal code and outlying-character code match the independent reader.

limits: The KSH settlement-part categories do not establish a complete inventory of urban quarters.
Not-reviewed city references mean unknown coverage, not zero quarters.
The current complete Budapest name reference does not itself supply complete source-supported quarter geometries.
The name inventory contains no geometry and cannot assign an address to a quarter.

countryOsm.scope: Entire Hungary extract; named place=suburb|quarter|neighbourhood polygons/nodes and named admin_level=9|10|11 polygons. Completeness applies to processing this selection, not to real-world neighborhood coverage.
countryOsm.rejectionMeaning: No valid assembled source polygon; rejection alone does not distinguish all source-data and extract-edge causes.
limits: The 440 raw source polygons include 23 Budapest district polygons and 21 unresolved features. They are not 440 verified Hungarian quarters.
Non-district administrative subdivisions and named place polygons require semantic review and may overlap or represent different area categories.
Named points establish names and locations, not extents.
All country source polygons remain unreviewed; valid rings and municipality containment do not verify the quarter boundary.
The 45 planning units are not 45 fine urban-neighborhood polygons.
Calibration residuals measure registration fit, not independent interior boundary accuracy.
Orbánhegy contains five inferred connectors totaling 304.85 m; Apostolhegy has an unresolved legal-junction interpretation; Péterimajor uses a land-use proxy.
Nyíregyháza raster registration residuals reach about 187 m at the 95th percentile and 586 m maximum.
Békéscsaba uses an extruded/shadowed source map with morphological closing; recorded spatial uncertainty is at least 80 m.
Map-derived source reuse rights remain unresolved. The manual review does not establish surveyed/legal boundaries, address assignment, or complete city coverage.
integrationLimits: Tata Tóváros remains quarantined by the conservative loader (manual_hole_outside_shell); all nine raw Tata source features are preserved.
Szombathely Belváros is a duplicate; the primary catalog prefers the existing machine-source polygon.

benchmark.reference: Actual same-PBF OSM quarter polygons matched by point name and containment; geometric-fit reference, not independent official legal ground truth.

exportedGeometryObservations.partitionMetricLimit: Near-zero pre-export metric partition differences are not proof that the final WGS84-exported cells cover the municipality exactly.

limits: One map label in one physical barrier cell does not establish the quarter extent.

The estimator flattens line intersections and discards bridge/tunnel/layer distinctions when constructing cells; grade-separated crossings and dual carriageways can produce irrelevant or sliver cells.
Overall and Budapest median IoU fail the prototype's 0.5 QA threshold. A favorable result from only 26 Debrecen pairs does not validate another city or the country.
No Szeged quarter-reference benchmark exists in this run.
Physical cells must remain a separate research artifact and must not be counted as source-supported quarters.
